I need a very thorough analysis of everything in this codebase (the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa) related to the "US-INTL" site — this is the "US International" storefront (one of Zimmermann's 8 storefronts across 6 regions: AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME).

Search broadly for how this site is identified and configured. Look for identifiers like: "US-INTL", "us-intl", "usintl", "US International", "us_intl", "USI", and any SITE_ID / locale / currency / URL-prefix mapping that would correspond to the US international storefront.

Specifically investigate and report:
1. **Site configuration** — check `config/sites.js`, `config/default.js`, and any `config/*.js` for the site definition (id, alias, l10n locales, currencies, URL path/prefix). Report the exact site id and how it's distinguished from US domestic.
2. **Regional docs** — read `.docs/prd/regional.md` in full and report everything it says about US-INTL: routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, consent/Didomi defaults, currency, locales, marketing opt-in behaviour, and any integration boundaries (Global-e, etc.).
3. **Any other .docs references** — grep all of `.docs/` for US international / US-INTL and summarize what each hit says (integration docs, memory files, PRDs).
4. **Code references** — any component, hook, util, route, fixture, or test that branches on or references the US international site specifically.
5. **E2E fixtures** — check `e2e/fixtures/` and any SITE_ID-keyed fixtures for a US-INTL entry.

Report exact file paths and line numbers for every finding, and quote the relevant snippets. Be exhaustive — I want to know every place US-INTL appears and every way it differs from the other storefronts. Do not modify any files; this is read-only research.

3	_Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13)._
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)
8	
9	**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).
10	
11	> **Status (2026-07-10):** REG-005 is **updated** — the US is now **two separate SFCC sites**: a US domestic site (`/us/`, SFCC checkout only) and a US international site (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout only). This supersedes the 2026-06-11 single-site decision. Rationale: managing Global-e complexity is simpler with a dedicated site boundary; inventory pooling and reporting can be handled at the SFCC realm level. **New site IDs require confirmation in Business Manager** — `ZimmermannUSIntl` is the working name for the international site.
12	
13	Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).
14	
15	11 active locales across the 8 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international remain separate storefronts (REG-006). US domestic and US international are now separate storefronts (REG-005, updated 2026-07-10).
16	
17	SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):
18	
19	| Locale           | SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                     | URL prefix                     | Local currency         | Checkout owner          |
20	| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
21	| AU (+ Oceania)   | `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                             | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD                    | SFCC (REG-003)          |
22	| UK               | `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                          | `/uk/`                         | GBP                    | SFCC (REG-004)          |
23	| US domestic      | `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                          | `/us/`                         | USD                    | SFCC (REG-005)          |
24	| US international | `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(confirm locale in BM)_ | `/en-ca/`                      | USD                    | Global-e (REG-005)      |
25	| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB`                          | `/en-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |

41	### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

60	## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)
61	
62	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
63	- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
64	- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
65	- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
66	- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
67	- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
68	- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
69	- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

75	- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
76	- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
77	- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)
78	
79	Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

84	
85	- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
86	- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
87	- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
88	- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
89	- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. 1	# SFCC Business Manager ↔ PWA Kit Region/Locale Sync — Findings & Implementation
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Zimmermann's storefront config (which SFCC sites exist, what locales/currencies each
6	serves, what URL prefix each uses) originates in Salesforce Business Manager (BM) but has
7	to be manually re-created inside this PWA Kit repo for the storefront to route and render
8	each region correctly. This document started as investigation into how that sync worked
9	and where it was fragile, then became the design + implementation record once the SCAPI
10	sync option (formerly "Option A" below) was actually built out. **Status: implemented and
11	locally testing as of this update** — see "What's actually built" below. The known
12	7-vs-8-storefront count drift (US domestic/international split, per
13	`.docs/prd/regional.md` REG-005) is a separate, smaller fix and deliberately not detailed
14	here — it's easy and will be picked up on its own later.
15	
16	## How sync worked before this PR — five hand-maintained locations, and this is Salesforce's documented pattern
17	
18	BM config was manually transcribed into five locations (six files, two of which are
19	grouped pairs) that had to stay in lockstep: `.docs/prd/regional.md` (requirements source
20	of truth); `config/sites.js` + `config/default.js` together (the config PWA Kit actually
21	runs on — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (a second, independent config
22	keyed by URL slug — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (SFCC↔Contentful
23	mapping); and `e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` together (Playwright fixtures). See
24	"What's actually built" below for how this looks now — `sites.js`/`default.js` are joined
25	by `sites.generated.js`/`sites.overlay.js`, and `countries.ts`/`contentfulMapping.ts`/the
26	e2e fixtures each gained their own generated + overlay split too.
27	
28	This is not a Zimmermann anti-pattern — Salesforce's own docs confirm `config/sites.js`
29	exists specifically to be manually kept in sync with Business Manager, and that
30	`l10n.supportedLocales` "must match" BM's locale settings, by design. Salesforce's newer
31	"Storefront Next" template consolidates this to one file (`config.server.ts`'s
32	`commerce.sites`) plus an env-var override, but even there `i18n.supportedLngs` still has
33	to be manually kept aligned with `commerce.sites[].supportedLocales` — the sync surface
34	shrinks, but a fully single-source-of-truth config doesn't exist anywhere Salesforce
35	documents, current or next-gen.
36	
37	The one file that actually determines whether a region loads correctly at runtime is
38	`config/sites.js`: `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (`AppConfig.restore`)
39	resolves site+locale per request by scanning every site's `l10n.supportedLocales` for a
40	match against the URL's locale segment, and **falls back silently to the AU default site
41	if nothing matches — no error, no log**. Everything else (`countries.ts`,
42	`contentfulMapping.ts`, e2e fixtures) is a secondary mirror of whatever `sites.js` says.
43	
44	## Option A — a SCAPI sync job to replace part of the manual transcription
45	
46	OCAPI (the old Data API path for reading site config) is officially deprecated (April
47	2026, ~2-year patch-only tail). The relevant current SCAPI endpoint is confirmed:
48	
49	- **`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/configurations?siteId={siteId}`**
50	  (`configuration/shopper-configurations/v1`, confirmed via
51	  `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s generated types — this is a real, typed client
52	  method already available in a dependency this repo has, not a new package).
53	- Returns a `siteConfiguration` entry covering **name, status, currencies, and locales**
54	  per site — exactly what `config/sites.js` needs to stay correct.
55	- **Uses the same SLAS shopper credentials already used elsewhere in this repo.** This is
56	  materially better than it first looked — the initially-found `sfcc.preferences`/`sfcc.sites`
57	  Admin APIs would have needed a brand-new Account Manager client_credentials setup;
58	  Shopper Configurations needs no new credential class at all.
59	- **One call per site — there's no org-wide "list all sites" call.** A sync script needs
60	  to already know the site ID list (which it does — it's the thing being verified).
61	- Explicitly documented as "highly cacheable" — this is designed for infrequent polling,
62	  not a per-request call. **Confirms the user's instinct: this should be a sync job run on
63	  demand or on a schedule (e.g. a `scripts/sfcc/` script analogous to
64	  `scripts/contentful/setup/detectDrift.mjs`, run manually before a release or on a cron),
65	  never called at runtime from the storefront itself.**
66	
67	**What this closes, and what it doesn't:** a sync job here can _verify_ `config/sites.js`
68	against live BM (site status, locales, currencies) and flag drift — but it can't safely
69	_auto-write_ `config/sites.js`, since that file is Tier 1 and any write still needs
70	Integration-team review. Realistic shape: a `detect:regional-drift`-style script that
71	exits non-zero and prints a diff when BM and `config/sites.js` disagree, run manually or
72	in CI, not an auto-fix. This directly addresses the "5 files, easy to miss one" concern —
73	it wouldn't eliminate the files, but it would catch drift in the most important one
74	(`config/sites.js`) without hand-comparing against a BM screenshot.
75	
76	**Update: built, and taken further than originally scoped here** — see "What's actually
77	built" below. Rather than a read-only drift-checker, the user (a verified
78	`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` member) opted to have the script actually write the
79	derived config, extended to all four hand-maintained files, not just `config/sites.js`.
80	
81	### Could this go further than a drift-check — e.g. generate/override `sites.js` instead of just diffing it?
82	
83	We checked whether Salesforce's newer "Storefront Next" template's approach (one config
84	file, overridable via a single env var, `PUBLIC__app__commerce__sites` — see
85	`zimmermann-sfn`'s `docs/README-CONFIG.md`) is portable here. **It is not, directly** —
86	that's a Vite-build-time mechanism specific to Storefront Next's SDK generation. The
87	current PWA Kit's config loader (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.server.js`,
88	`getConfig()`) does whole-file selection only (`config/{tier}.js` → `config/default.js`
89	via `cosmiconfigSync`, keyed off `DEPLOY_TARGET`) — there is no env-var merge step
90	anywhere in it. A same-*spirit* mechanism could be hand-built from scratch (`config/sites.js`
91	is just a plain `module.exports`, so nothing stops it reading an env var or a generated
92	file itself) — but that would be new engineering inspired by sfn, not a port of anything,
93	and MRT's practical env-var size limits for a multi-KB JSON blob are unconfirmed.
94	
95	More importantly, **even a generated/overridden `sites.js` would not eliminate the
96	hand-maintenance, only shrink part of it.** The Shopper Configurations response can supply
97	locale-ID and currency truth, but it has no concept of Zimmermann's `alias` field (the URL
98	prefix, e.g. `fr-eu`) or the `sfccSiteId` override (how the 4 fake EU sites point at one
99	real SFCC site) — both are pure PWA-Kit/Zimmermann routing concepts that don't exist in
100	Business Manager or SCAPI at all. So the realistic ceiling is a **hybrid**: SCAPI-sourced
101	locale/currency data plus a permanently hand-maintained small overlay for routing/alias
102	data — and a script that *writes* any part of `config/sites.js` (even generated) is a
103	bigger governance ask than the read-only drift-checker above, needing explicit
104	Integration-team design sign-off before any code is written, not just implementation
105	approval.
106	
107	**Honest framing:** this makes locale/currency drift *catchable, and eventually
108	automatable*. It does not make `config/sites.js` *not-hand-maintained* — URL routing config
109	stays manual permanently, because it structurally isn't a Business Manager/SCAPI concept
110	to sync from. Recommend treating "drift-check script" (read-only) and "generated overlay"
111	(writes, needs sign-off) as two separate, sequential asks — not one.
112	
113	**Side finding, unrelated to this plan:** `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` is present
114	in this repo's `package.json`/`node_modules` even though nothing here uses it (this repo
115	runs `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`/`pwa-kit-runtime` v3.18.0, a different SDK generation
116	entirely). Worth understanding why it's there before it causes confusion later — out of
117	scope for this document.
118	
119	## What's actually built
120	
121	The "generate + hand-maintained overlay" pattern was extended to **all four** files, not
122	just `config/sites.js` — the user's explicit call was that BM changes should flow to every
123	consuming file when the sync script runs, not just the highest-leverage one.
124	
125	### Files
126	
127	| Kind | File | Notes |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| Script | `scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs` | `npm run sync:regional-config` (`-- --dry-run` for a no-write preview) |
130	| Generated (rewritten every sync) | `config/sites.generated.js` | per real SFCC site: status/defaultLocale/defaultCurrency/supportedCurrencies/supportedLocales |
131	| Generated | `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` | per URL slug: sfccSiteId/locale/currency |
132	| Generated | `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts` | SUPPORTED_LOCALES + SITE_LOCALES per PWA site id |
133	| Generated | `e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js` | per e2e fixture key: locale/currency/currencySymbol/siteId — self-contained, no merge needed downstream |
134	| Hand-maintained overlay | `config/sites.overlay.js` | id/sfccSiteId/locale-id/alias per PWA site (10 entries) |
135	| Hand-maintained overlay | `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js` | fixture key → PWA site id (10 entries) |
136	| Hand-maintained overlay | inline in `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` | shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion per slug — not a separate file, since `countries.ts` isn't on the Hard-Rule-4 absolute list and could just be edited directly |
137	| Consumer (thin merge — written once by hand, **not** touched by `npm run sync:regional-config`) | `config/sites.js`, `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `e2e/fixtures/site.js` | Imports the generated + overlay files at load time; only needs a manual edit again if the merge *logic* itself changes, not when BM data changes |
138	
139	### What the live API actually looks like (worth preserving — nothing in Salesforce's docs states this)
140	
141	The Shopper Configurations response is **not** the nested object the SDK's `any`-typed
142	field suggests. It's a flat array of `{configurationType, id, value}` entries — one per
143	field — mixing `siteConfiguration` entries (`id`/`name`/`status`/`timezone`/
144	`defaultCurrency`/`allowedCurrencies`/`defaultLocale`/`allowedLocales`) with unrelated
145	`globalConfiguration` entries (`SalesforcePaymentsAllowed`, `my_domain`). Field names differ
146	from every guess made before seeing a real response: `allowedCurrencies` not `currencies`,
147	`allowedLocales` not `locales`. `allowedLocales` entries are rich objects
148	(`{id, country, displayName, ...}`) with **no per-locale currency field** and always
149	include a placeholder `{id: 'default', ...}` entry that isn't real. Since every site here
150	uses one currency across all its locales, each real locale is assigned the site's own
151	`defaultCurrency` rather than a (non-existent) per-locale value.
152	
153	### Auth gotcha (also undocumented, cost real debugging time)
154	
155	The guest `client_credentials` token request fails with `400 "Guest token requires a
156	channel_id parameter"` unless a `channel_id` (the SFCC site ID) is included in the token
157	request body — and a token is scoped to exactly one site, so the script requests a fresh
158	token per site rather than one shared token. Separately, an `401 "incorrect client type"`
159	error meant the existing SLAS client (used for the storefront's normal shopper login) had
160	no `sfcc.shopper-configurations` scope enabled — added via the SLAS Admin UI at
161	`https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/shopper/auth-admin/v1/ui/` (not a
162	generic Account Manager screen). Watch for the near-identical, wrong scope name
163	`sfcc.shopper-configuations` (missing an 'r') if this ever needs re-deriving from a search.
164	
165	### Formatting
166	
167	`JSON.stringify`'s output (double quotes, no trailing commas) fails this repo's
168	`prettier/prettier` eslint rule — the script runs `npx eslint --fix` on each file it writes
169	rather than hand-rolling a formatter that duplicates `.prettierrc`.
170	
171	### Bug found and fixed along the way
172	
173	`e2e/fixtures/customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map only had a single `eu` key and was missing
174	`euIntl` entirely — pre-existing, unrelated to this work, but became a live mismatch once
175	`site.js` gained the correct 4-way EU split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus `euIntl`.
176	Fixed with per-locale addresses (Berlin/Paris/Rome/Madrid/Zurich) so all 10 keys line up
177	across both files.
178	
179	### Verification run (2026-07-17)
180	
181	`node --check` on every new/changed `.js`/`.mjs`, a functional `require()` smoke test of
182	`e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` + `config/sites.js`, `npx eslint` (clean) and
183	`npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) across every touched file. Followed by a local `npm start` pass
184	hitting all ten regional URLs and confirming each resolved the expected site/locale
185	(root `/` → AU/`en`, `/us/` → US/`en-US`, `/uk/` → UK/`en-GB`, `/en-eu/` `/fr-eu/` `/it-eu/`
186	`/es-eu/` → the four EU locales, `/en-ch/` → EU Intl/`en-CH`, `/hk/` → HK/`en-HK`,
187	`/en-ae/` → ME/`en-AE`) — this is what caught the `defaultLocale` bug documented below.
188	
189	### Known current-state quirk (expected, not a bug)
190	
191	The dev realm's live data currently returns `HK: USD` and `ME: EUR`, not the documented
192	production targets `HKD`/`AED` — almost certainly this dev sandbox not being fully
193	configured with production currencies yet. This is exactly the kind of drift this pipeline
194	now surfaces automatically; once BM is corrected, re-running `npm run sync:regional-config`
195	will pull the right values into all four generated files in one pass.
196	
197	### Real bug found in local testing (fixed)
198	
199	`config/sites.js`'s merge logic originally set `l10n.defaultLocale: source.defaultLocale`
200	— SCAPI's **site-level** default for the real SFCC site, not scoped to the one locale a
201	given PWA site actually supports. This crashed `npm start` immediately: BM's
202	`ZimmermannAU` default is `en-AU`, but the `ZimmermannAU` PWA site's overlay only lists
203	`en` — so `defaultLocale` pointed at a locale absent from `supportedLocales`,
204	`_app-config`'s `AppConfig.restore` failed both locale lookups, and crashed on
205	`undefined.alias`. Same bug would have hit `ZimmermannEUfr`/`EUit`/`EUes` too (BM's shared
206	`ZimmermannEU` default `en-GB` only matches `EUen`). **Fix:** `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`
207	instead — every PWA site has exactly one locale in its overlay by design, so that locale
208	*is* its default; SCAPI's notion of "default" belongs to the real SFCC site, not to
209	Zimmermann's per-locale PWA site split, and should never have been used here.
210	
211	### Open item carried over from the original US-split design
212	
213	`countries.ts`'s hand-maintained overlay still has an `en-ca` (US international) entry
214	defined, but it's excluded from the live `COUNTRIES` export by construction — there's no
215	matching entry in `config/sites.overlay.js` yet, since `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID is
216	still unconfirmed in BM (see "Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation" below,
217	unchanged).
218	
219	## Option B — consolidate the EU 4-way site split (separate from the above, no framework migration needed)
220	
221	Zimmermann currently models EU domestic as **4 fake PWA sites**
222	(`ZimmermannEUen`/`fr`/`it`/`es`), each with one locale, all sharing one real
223	`sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'`. We asked whether this split is actually required by the
224	current PWA Kit SDK, or self-imposed. **Confirmed self-imposed, not required** —
225	Salesforce's own shipped reference config (`RefArchGlobal` in the upstream `pwa-kit` repo)
226	has a single site with **16 locales** in one `supportedLocales` array. The underlying SDK
227	functions (`getConfigMatcher`, `getLocaleByReference`, `resolveLocaleFromUrl` in
228	`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/site-utils.js`) all operate generically
229	over locale arrays of any length — there's no 1-locale-per-site limitation in the SDK
230	itself.
231	
232	**But this is not a trivial merge, and it interacts with other things in this document —
233	read before acting on either:**
234	
235	- **The comment in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`** explaining why the
236	  custom resolution hack exists ("because `url.site` is `'none'`...") **is factually wrong
237	  for the current config** — `config/default.js` actually sets `url.site: 'path'`. This is
238	  a small, separate doc/comment cleanup, unrelated to whether consolidation happens.
239	- **The custom `_app-config` override should be kept, not removed, if consolidating** — it
240	  currently produces the same result as the stock SDK function for the 4-fake-site model
241	  (effectively redundant today), but a live empirical test found the stock SDK's
242	  locale-matching regex has a real prefix-collision bug (`fr` matches before `fr-eu` in its
243	  alternation list, truncating the match) that the _consolidated_ single-site model would
244	  hit — and the custom hack's `id`-or-`alias` matching happens to already tolerate it.
245	  Removing the hack while consolidating would break `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`.
246	- **Outbound URL generation needs rework, not just config.** `createUrlTemplate` decides
247	  the URL's site-vs-locale segment from `site.alias`; a consolidated site has no per-locale
248	  alias, so URLs would need to be generated from the locale segment instead — a real
249	  logic change in how `locals.buildUrl` is constructed, not a `sites.js`-only edit.
250	- **This conflict is now resolved in favor of the 4-site model — reversing it is the cost
251	  of pursuing Option B.** `e2e/fixtures/site.js` (and its generation pipeline, and
252	  `e2e/fixtures/customers.js`) now use the 4-key split (`enEu`/`frEu`/`itEu`/`esEu`) plus
253	  `euIntl`, matching today's `config/sites.js`. If EU consolidation happens later, all of
254	  `e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js`, the sync script's e2e-derivation logic, and
255	  `customers.js`'s `ADDRESSES` map would need to collapse back to a single `eu` key —
256	  budget for that alongside the URL-generation rework below.
257	- `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` needs **no structural change** either way — it's
258	  already keyed by URL slug with `sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'` on every EU entry (now via
259	  `countries.generated.ts`, but the shape is the same), effectively pre-consolidated.
260	- `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` would collapse
261	  from 4 keys to 1 (`ZimmermannEU: ['en-GB','fr','it','es']`) if consolidating — this is
262	  now script-derived rather than hand-written, so the change would happen automatically on
263	  the next sync once `config/sites.overlay.js` is consolidated, not as a separate manual
264	  edit.
265	
266	**Net effect if pursued:** `config/sites.js`'s EU block goes from 4 objects to 1 (one
267	fewer thing to keep in sync across the 5-file chain for EU specifically), but the
268	resolution/URL-generation code doesn't get simpler — it stays and does real work. This is
269	worth doing for config-sync hygiene, but it's a scoped piece of engineering work with
270	real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case), not a free cleanup.
271	
272	## Where this leaves the earlier US-split remediation
273	
274	Still pending BM confirming `ZimmermannUSIntl`'s real site ID and locale ID — unaffected by
275	either the sync pipeline or the EU-consolidation question. Slightly easier now than
276	originally drafted: adding the new site to `config/sites.overlay.js` and its overlay entry
277	in `countries.ts` no longer needs a direct edit to the absolute-blocked `config/sites.js`
278	(that file is now just merge logic, regenerated automatically). **`config/default.js`'s
279	`siteAliases` map still needs a manual entry (`ZimmermannUSIntl: 'en-ca'`) and remains
280	absolutely off-limits regardless of approver status** — that one edit still has to be made
281	by hand, by a human, per `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4.
282	
283	## Status
284	
285	- **Option A (SCAPI sync pipeline): implemented**, extended to all four files per the
286	  user's decision, currently in local testing. See "What's actually built" above.
287	- **Option B (EU 4-way consolidation): still undecided, not implemented.** Worth doing for
288	  config-sync hygiene, but real behavioural risk (URL generation, a regex edge case) and
289	  now a wider blast radius than originally scoped — it also touches the e2e fixture
290	  generation pipeline built for Option A, not just `config/sites.js` and `countries.ts`.

# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.

PWA responsibilities:

- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
- Handling the order-completion return path

Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.

## 2. Checkout ownership matrix

| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |

Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.

> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
        │
        ▼
PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
        │
        ▼
Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
        │
        ▼
Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
        │
        ▼
SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
        │
        ▼
PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
        │
        ▼

## 6. Multi-region behaviour

`includedRegionCodes` is set per active storefront to mirror the country-to-storefront routing:

| Storefront | Included region codes |
|---|---|
| AU | AU plus Oceania (NZ, FJ, NC, …) |
| US (`/us/`) | US, PR |
| US international (`/en-ca/`) | All Americas excluding US (pre-handoff capture; Global-e takes over inside its iframe) |

| EU domestic | DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, BE, … (the full EU domestic list) |
| EU international | Non-EU Europe plus Africa long tail (pre-handoff) |
| HK | HK plus the APAC long tail |
